title: Define default gate thresholds for Dedicated staged rollouts (v1) + configurability policy
creator: Lauren Bishop
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description: We need to land a set of Redwood-default rollout gate thresholds for Dedicated reserved pools that is (1) aligned to SLOs and error budget policy, (2) stable across regions/hardware variability, and (3) implementable in the policy engine with deterministic evaluation. This ticket defines the default thresholds by tier/region, and explicitly documents what is configurable vs fixed for v1 (beta/GA).
content:
Context
- Dedicated staged rollouts introduces promotion gates that can automatically pass/fail a stage based on objective signals (latency, errors, saturation, GPU health, OOM, drops/429). Dedicated customers are explicitly asking for “safer upgrades” but we must avoid over-fitting to individual workloads in v1.
- This ticket drives alignment across Product (Dedicated + Console), SRE, Infra/Fleet signals, and Policy Engine on:
  1) the default set of gates enabled per stage
  2) pass/fail thresholds + evaluation windows / minimum samples
  3) which dimensions are tier- or region-specific
  4) what customers can configure in v1 (and what remains Redwood-fixed)

Goals / success criteria
- A single documented “Default Gate Profile (v1)” that:
  - SRE signs off on for paging/noise + SLO alignment
  - Infra signs off on for capacity/headroom + fleet signal reliability
  - Policy Engine can implement without needing per-customer special cases
  - Console can present clearly (what was evaluated, why pass/fail)
- Clear statement of configurability:
  - “Can configure” (customer admin) vs “Redwood operator only” vs “fixed”
  - Identify any tier-level overrides (e.g., Enterprise vs Standard) and when those apply
- Output should be durable enough to go into:
  - ADR: gate evaluation signals and thresholds
  - Runbook: oncall actions for failed/unknown gates
  - Console copy: default thresholds and guidance

Non-goals
- Creating a fully custom per-customer gate builder UI
- Supporting arbitrary custom metrics (beyond Redwood-defined signals) in v1
- Finalizing quality-regression gates for every model/workload (we will scope quality gates to “optional / operator-enabled” for beta unless the evals harness integration is stable)

Proposed default gate set (v1)
Applies to each stage promotion check unless otherwise noted.

Gate A: Error rate (5xx + model/runtime errors)
- Signal: request_error_rate = (5xx + inference_failures) / total_requests
- Default threshold:
  - Pass if <= 0.25% for stage traffic (aggregated)
  - Warn band: 0.25%–0.5% (does not fail in v1; Console shows warning)
  - Fail if > 0.5%
- Evaluation window: 10 minutes rolling
- Minimum samples: 1,000 requests OR 50,000 tokens generated (whichever comes first)
- Rationale: protects against bad runtime builds and model config regressions without being overly sensitive to low-volume canary traffic.

Gate B: Latency regression (p95 + p99)
- Signal: end-to-end request latency for Dedicated pool route (includes queueing + inference)
- Default thresholds:
  - Pass if p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.15 AND absolute p95 <= tier_cap_p95
  - Pass if p99 <= baseline_p99 * 1.20 AND absolute p99 <= tier_cap_p99
- Tier caps (initial proposal):
  - Standard Dedicated: tier_cap_p95 = 1.8s, tier_cap_p99 = 3.5s
  - Enterprise Dedicated: tier_cap_p95 = 1.5s, tier_cap_p99 = 3.0s
- Evaluation window: 15 minutes rolling
- Baseline definition (v1): previous stable stage (or last completed rollout) for same pool + same primary route; if unavailable, fall back to 7-day median for same pool.
- Minimum samples: 300 requests
- Notes:
  - For small / bursty workloads, the “absolute cap” prevents baseline being too lenient.
  - If baseline is missing AND samples < min, gate = UNKNOWN (blocks promotion) unless operator override is used.

Gate C: Saturation / headroom (avoid capacity starvation)
- Signals (any failing triggers fail):
  - gpu_utilization_avg > 92% (sustained)
  - queue_depth_p95 > 2x baseline_queue_depth_p95 OR queue_wait_p95 > 250ms
  - batcher_backpressure_events increasing (derivative) above threshold
- Default threshold:
  - Fail if sustained saturation (>= 5 minutes within the 15m window)
  - Pass otherwise
- Evaluation window: 15 minutes rolling
- Baseline: last stable stage
- Rationale: prevents canary partition from starving and causing 429s / queue spikes (observed in early beta).

Gate D: Drop/429 rate
- Signal: (429 + request_dropped) / total_requests
- Default threshold:
  - Fail if > 0.2% over 10 minutes
  - Warn if 0.1%–0.2%
- Minimum samples: 1,000 requests
- Rationale: explicit protection against over-partitioning + routing starvation.

Gate E: OOM / GPU health
- Signals:
  - oom_rate: OOM events / total_requests
  - gpu_health_degraded: node taints, ECC spikes, thermal throttling (fleet signal)
- Default thresholds:
  - Fail if oom_rate > 0.05% over 15 minutes OR > 2 OOMs in 15 minutes (whichever triggers first)
  - Fail if gpu_health_degraded > 0 for canary partition for > 3 minutes (within a 15m window)
- Notes:
  - GPU health freshness requirement: metrics must be <= 2 minutes stale; if stale, gate = UNKNOWN.

Gate F (optional / operator-enabled in beta): Quality regression
- Signal: eval score delta for the canary variant vs baseline on configured prompt set
- Default threshold:
  - Fail if score drops > 2.0% relative on “primary” eval metric (per model family)
- Evaluation window: last 30 minutes (asynchronous)
- V1 plan: operator enables this gate only for customers with existing eval harness coverage; not customer-configurable in GA v1.

Stage-specific notes
- For Stage 1 (e.g., 1% or 1 replica), minimum sample constraints are the biggest practical blocker. Proposal:
  - Still enforce min samples, but allow “time-based completion” (e.g., 30 minutes) to satisfy min samples for low-QPS pools.
  - If neither min samples nor max time met, gate remains UNKNOWN and stage is held.

What is configurable vs fixed (v1 policy proposal)
Customer-configurable (Dedicated customer admin)
- Stage plan shape: choose from a small set of presets (1/10/50/100; 5/25/50/100; replica-based for small pools) (already tracked in PRD scope; included here for clarity)
- Promotion mode: manual vs automatic promotion (automatic = evaluate gates continuously and promote when all pass)
- Hold/abort: customer can manually hold or abort if they have rollout permissions

Configurable by Redwood operator only (via admin tooling)
- Threshold profile selection: Standard vs Enterprise profile
- Per-gate enable/disable (e.g., turning off GPU health if a region signal is temporarily unreliable)
- Quality gate enablement
- Temporary overrides to thresholds with a required “reason” string (must be written to audit log)

Fixed in v1 (not configurable)
- Gate definitions and signal sources (to preserve determinism and avoid query/cardinality issues)
- Evaluation windows and staleness rules (to avoid noisy behavior and inconsistent Console explanations)
- Fail-open vs fail-closed semantics under missing metrics: default = fail-closed (UNKNOWN blocks promotion) with explicit override pathway

Region/tier nuance
- Primary question: do we need region-specific threshold adjustments?
  - SRE preference so far: keep thresholds consistent across regions; rely on baseline-relative checks + absolute tier caps.
  - Infra note: some regions have higher variance due to GPU SKU mix; region-specific caps risk “hiding” systemic issues.
- Proposal: no region-specific thresholds in v1, except:
  - Known-impairment allowlist in ops playbook (operator can temporarily select “Relaxed profile” during incident response with explicit audit logging).

Open questions to resolve in this ticket
1) Confirm tier caps for latency (p95/p99) with SRE (Sean/Rafael) and Dedicated PM (Lauren). Are caps too strict for long-context customers? If so, do we scope caps by route type (chat vs embeddings) rather than by tier?
2) Minimum sample policy: requests vs tokens. Do we standardize on both (OR) as proposed? Telemetry feasibility (Logan) to confirm token counts available with stage tags at low cost.
3) Queue/saturation metrics: which is the most reliable cross-runtime indicator? (queue_wait_p95 vs queue_depth_p95 vs backpressure counters)
4) 429/drops threshold: is 0.2% too tight for some bursty clients? Alternative: align to error budget burn rather than absolute.
5) How to represent WARN vs FAIL in v1 gating UI: do WARNs block auto-promotion or only surface as “risky”? (Current proposal: WARN does not block promotion, but is visible and triggers a notification.)

Implementation notes / handoff requirements
- Policy engine needs a “gate profile” concept referenced by rollout plan (default: Standard).
- Console needs to render gate evidence consistently:
  - time window
  - observed value
  - threshold/baseline
  - pass/warn/fail/unknown state
- Audit requirements:
  - Any override (force-promote, relaxed profile, disabling a gate) must include actor + reason.

Progress updates (most recent first)
2025-03-14 (Paula Mendes)
- Synced with Rafael Mendes + Sean Gallagher: strong preference for fail-closed on missing/stale metrics; override allowed but must be audited and should page oncall if used outside incident window.
- Captured incident learnings: early beta canary caused 429s due to effective capacity reduction; this supports having an explicit 429/drop gate and saturation guardrails.
- Action: incorporate SRE feedback into final threshold table and share for sign-off.

2025-03-07 (Paula Mendes)
- Reviewed telemetry tagging status with Logan Wright: stage_id tagging exists but cardinality constraints mean we should keep the gate queries fixed + allowlisted.
- Tentative agreement: use request count for min sample; token-based min sample as optional if token_count is reliably tagged in all code paths.

2025-02-20 (Lauren Bishop)
- Added customer quotes to PM-812; recurring ask is “don’t let a pool upgrade silently degrade latency for 20 minutes.” This suggests windows <= 15m for latency/saturation.

Acceptance criteria
- A final “Default Gate Profile (v1)” section agreed by:
  - SRE (Sean/Rafael) and Observability standards (Allison) on thresholds/windows/alerts
  - Infra (Vanessa/Irene) on saturation/headroom signals and small pool constraints
  - Policy engine lead (Jordan) on determinism + missing data behavior
- Clear v1 configurability matrix (customer vs operator vs fixed) with copy suitable for Console tooltip/help text
- Link to the final doc/ADR section where thresholds are recorded (to be added once published)

Next steps
- Paula: post the updated threshold table + configurability matrix to #eng-sre and #eng-platform for final sign-off (by 2025-03-18)
- Lauren: confirm tier definitions for “Standard vs Enterprise Dedicated” as it relates to latency caps (by 2025-03-19)

comments: 2025-03-14 Paula Mendes: SRE wants fail-closed for UNKNOWN gates; override must be audited + preferably restricted to incident windows. Please ensure Console copy doesn’t imply the system is “broken” when it’s just missing metrics.

2025-03-10 Sean Gallagher: Error/latency gates look sane; be careful with min sample for 1% stage on low QPS. Recommend a max time in stage before requiring manual decision, otherwise we’ll get stuck rollouts.

2025-03-07 Logan Wright: We can provide stage-tagged request counts everywhere; token counts are available in most paths but verify streaming edge cases before making it a hard requirement for min samples.

2025-02-18 Vanessa Ortiz: Saturation should incorporate queue wait; raw GPU util can be misleading with kernel fusion changes. Also make sure the 1-replica canary doesn’t violate minimum headroom rules for small reservations.
